questions.q: Who decides to trigger this chapter's unannounced DR drill, and why?
options: The DBA team schedules it themselves, as another routine test
Azure automatically triggers it on a schedule
It's triggered randomly by the Data Factory pipeline
Overlook's leadership — the same board that mandated this project in Lesson 1 — triggers it without advance warning, specifically to find out whether the runbook holds up under realistic pressure
questions.explain: The point is testing the process under genuine pressure, not under conditions the DBA team controls and expects.

questions.q: What is this drill testing that Lesson 13's own controlled failover test could not?
options: Whether the DR runbook itself — the actual document, not memory of it — actually holds up when followed under realistic, unannounced pressure
Whether Bicep can deploy a new server
Whether the failover group technology works at all
Whether Data Factory's Copy activity works correctly
questions.explain: Lesson 13 proved the technology works under ideal conditions; this drill proves the documented process works under pressure.

questions.q: What is the correct first step the on-call DBA takes when the drill starts, according to this lesson?
options: Call the board for permission before doing anything
Check the runbook's trigger criteria to confirm the situation genuinely warrants a failover, not a brief blip to wait out
Immediately run the failover command from memory
Skip straight to the communication plan
questions.explain: The runbook's trigger criteria section exists exactly to make this judgment call correctly, documented, under pressure.

questions.q: What does this lesson identify as the wrong way to respond to a surprise drill, even if it would make the drill 'look clean'?
options: Communicating status while the failover is in progress
Improvising from memory, skipping steps that feel 'obviously fine,' or under-reporting a real problem to make the drill look clean
Opening the actual runbook document
Following the verification checklist
questions.explain: The value of the drill depends on treating it exactly like the real incident it's rehearsing for — shortcuts defeat the purpose.

questions.q: What does this lesson say a failover group that works perfectly, paired with a runbook nobody can follow under pressure, still represents?
options: A real gap — the technology working isn't the same as the documented process actually holding up when executed for real
Evidence the RPO target was set too low
Proof that runbooks are unnecessary
A complete success with nothing left to fix
questions.explain: This drill exists specifically to surface exactly that kind of gap between working technology and an unfollowable process.
